place: Title — resolution of the generalized Goodman conjecture
claim: The focused title refers to Conjecture 1, the unweighted coefficient bound for every admissible pole, Schwarz function and positive degree.

place: The normalized meromorphic map
claim: The function f is one-to-one and meromorphic in the unit disk, has a simple pole at a real point 0 < p < 1, and satisfies f(0) = 0 and f′(0) = 1.
source_words: meromorphic and one-to-one in the unit disk

place: The sharp bound before composition
claim: For n ≥ 1, the nth Taylor coefficient of f at zero has modulus at most Aₙ(p) = (1−p²ⁿ)/((1−p²)pⁿ⁻¹). The bound is sharp at every degree.
source_words: $a_n$ at the origin satisfy the sharp bound

place: Jenkins’s implication from Bieberbach’s conjecture
claim: Jenkins showed that Bieberbach’s conjecture implies the meromorphic coefficient bound. De Branges settled Bieberbach’s conjecture in 1985.
source_words: Goodman conjectured this bound, and Jenkins showed that it follows

place: Taylor coefficients of the subordinate map
claim: If h maps the disk holomorphically into itself and fixes zero, f∘h is holomorphic near zero even when it has poles elsewhere in the disk.
source_words: poles, but it is holomorphic near $0$

place: Origins and known cases of the generalized Goodman conjecture
claim: Avkhadiev and Wirths proposed the meromorphic analogue of Rogosinski’s conjecture in 2006 and named it in 2009. De Branges’s theorem settled the holomorphic analogue. Earlier meromorphic bounds covered n ≤ 2, n = 3 for p < 0.7, and n ≥ 4 for p < 1/(2n−2), with further results for special classes of f.
source_words: Their 2009 book named this the generalized Goodman

place: The unweighted bound in all degrees
claim: For every n ≥ 1 and 0 < p < 1, the nth coefficient of f∘h has modulus at most Aₙ(p). Equality at n ≥ 2 requires both the extremal f(z) = z/((1−pz)(1−z/p)) and a rotation h.

place: Two derivative conjectures of 2008
claim: Theorem 3 gives the sharp bounds conjectured by Avkhadiev and Wirths in 2008 for derivatives of order n ≥ 2 at finite values of a meromorphic map. Its source is the disk or a proper convex plane domain, and its target is a simply connected spherical domain omitting at least two points.
source_words: derivatives of a meromorphic map from the disk, or from a convex domain

place: The expanded companion
claim: The abstract points to an expanded version of the paper containing further results.

place: Three ingredients of the coefficient estimate
claim: For each coefficient index the transfer lemma supplies a holomorphic disk weight bounded by one. The slit map fixes zero and has positive Taylor coefficients in positive degrees. Robertson’s inequality bounds the odd coefficients used in the product estimate.

place: Scope of the Lean footnote
claim: The footnote reports verification of the eight numbered results in the focused paper, with four published inputs used where needed. These are Robertson’s odd-coefficient inequality, Bieberbach’s second-coefficient equality case, the Marx–Strohhäcker theorem, and the planar Riemann mapping theorem.
source_words: four published theorems, checked with \texttt{lake comparator}

place: Classification and keywords
claim: The primary 2020 MSC code is 30C50, with secondary codes 30C45 and 30C80. Keywords include meromorphic univalent functions, coefficient estimates, subordination, Schwarz–Pick inequalities, and the generalized Goodman conjecture.

place: The class S and coefficient notation
claim: S consists of the injective holomorphic maps F on the open unit disk 𝔻 with F(0) = 0 and F′(0) = 1. The symbol [wⁿ]g denotes the nth Taylor coefficient of g at zero.
source_words: the coefficient of $w^n$ in the Taylor expansion

place: De Branges’s bound for normalized univalent functions
claim: For every F in S and every n ≥ 1, |[wⁿ]F| ≤ n (de Branges, 1985, pp. 137–138).

place: The meromorphic class M(p)
claim: For real 0 < p < 1, M(p) consists of injective meromorphic maps on 𝔻 with their only pole simple and at p, normalized by f(0) = 0 and f′(0) = 1.
source_words: have a simple pole at $p$ and no other pole

place: The disk of the Taylor expansion
claim: Every f in M(p) is holomorphic on |z| < p, where its Taylor series has constant term zero and linear term z.
source_words: $|z|<p$, so it has a Taylor expansion

place: The coefficient estimate for M(p)
claim: For f in M(p) and n ≥ 1, |[zⁿ]f| ≤ Aₙ(p), with equality attained by fₚ.

place: Two expressions for the coefficient bound
claim: For n ≥ 1 and 0 < p < 1, Aₙ(p) = p¹⁻ⁿ(1+p²+⋯+p²ⁿ⁻²) = (1−p²ⁿ)/((1−p²)pⁿ⁻¹).

place: Uniqueness of the unweighted base extremal
claim: For each n ≥ 2, a function f in M(p) attains |[zⁿ]f| = Aₙ(p) exactly when f = fₚ on the disk.

place: The rational extremal with pole p
claim: The extremal is fₚ(z) = z/((1−pz)(1−z/p)), with spherical value ∞ at p.

place: Coefficients of the rational extremal
claim: For every n ≥ 1, [zⁿ]fₚ = Aₙ(p). The same function attains all the base bounds.

place: Goodman’s real-coefficient theorem and conjecture
claim: Goodman proved the base estimate when all coefficients are real and conjectured it for all f in M(p).
source_words: Goodman proved~\eqref{eq:An} when all the coefficients

place: Sources for Jenkins’s meromorphic reduction
claim: Jenkins derives the base bound from the Bieberbach conjecture and the equality characterization from its equality case. The paper cites Jenkins (pp. 25–27), Avkhadiev and Wirths (Section 2.3) and de Branges (p. 151).
source_words: Jenkins showed that it follows from the Bieberbach

place: Schwarz functions
claim: A Schwarz function is a holomorphic self-map h of 𝔻 with h(0) = 0. This includes the zero function.

place: Poles and regularity of the composition
claim: For f in M(p) and a Schwarz function h, f∘h is meromorphic on 𝔻 with poles exactly where h(z) = p. It is holomorphic on |z| < p.
source_words: It has a pole at every point where $h$ takes the value $p$

place: Loss of injectivity under subordination
claim: Even for f in M(p), f∘h can fail to be injective. For instance, h ≡ 0 gives a constant composite.
source_words: in general it is not one-to-one

place: Conjecture 1 — the generalized Goodman bound
claim: For every 0 < p < 1, every f in M(p), every Schwarz function h, and every n ≥ 1, |[zⁿ](f∘h)| ≤ Aₙ(p).

place: Geometric and coefficient formulations of the conjecture
claim: Avkhadiev and Wirths proposed inequality (5) after Theorem D in 2006, named the conjecture in their 2009 book (p. 132), and restated it for coefficients in 2013 (Conjecture 1, p. 143), with h(z) = zω(z) and |ω| ≤ 1.

place: Place of the conjecture in the Schwarz–Pick monograph
claim: Section 8.3 (pp. 131–138) of the 2009 monograph names the conjecture and devotes half the closing open-problems chapter to it alongside the Krzyż and angle conjectures.

place: Rogosinski’s holomorphic coefficient bound
claim: For F in S, every Schwarz function h, and n ≥ 1, |[zⁿ](F∘h)| ≤ n.

place: The limit as the pole approaches the circle
claim: For each fixed n ≥ 1, Aₙ(p) tends to n as p increases to 1.

place: Robertson’s inequality and Rogosinski’s conjecture
claim: Robertson’s odd-coefficient inequality yields Rogosinski’s bound for subordinates of functions in S. De Branges gives the odd-coefficient result on pp. 137–138, and Szapiel gives the subordination implication on p. 172.

place: Earlier bounds for the full meromorphic class
claim: Theorem 8.3 of Avkhadiev and Wirths’s 2009 book gives the bound for n = 2 and all 0 < p < 1, for n = 3 and p < 0.7, and for n ≥ 4 and p < 1/(2n−2).

place: Convex-complement coefficient bound
claim: Avkhadiev and Wirths (2007), Theorem 1, give the bound for every n and admissible p when the range has convex complement. The monograph also records it in Theorem 8.4.

place: Application to Bohr–Rogosinski inequalities
claim: Allu and Arora (2023), Lemma 4.1, use the concave-domain coefficient bound in their Bohr–Rogosinski argument for meromorphic subordination.

place: Earlier bounds for special meromorphic classes
claim: Avkhadiev and Wirths (2013) covered all degrees for two starlike-complement classes and noted the known real-coefficient case. Bhowmik and Parveen (2019) covered n ≥ 3 and p ≤ 1/3 for a subclass defined by a differential inequality.
source_words: one of two classes of starlike sets

place: Counterexample for the deformed subclass conjecture
claim: Li, Ponnusamy and Wirths (2024) give a counterexample to a related coefficient conjecture with λ < 1 for the differential-inequality subclass, at n = 3 and large p.
source_words: subclass was recently disproved for $n=3$ and large $p$

place: Figure 1 — ranges of the earlier estimates
claim: The left panel shows Schwarz’s lemma for n = 1 and the sufficient ranges stated in the 2009 Theorem 8.3 for general f. For n = 3 its proof on p. 133 reaches 0.7088023…, including hatched points such as p = 0.705.

place: Figure 1 — coverage of Theorem 1
claim: The right panel represents the bound for all f in M(p), every 0 < p < 1, and every n ≥ 1, including the degrees beyond those displayed.

place: Figure 1 — how to read the shading
claim: The figure draws degrees 1 through 10. Solid shading on the left marks the stated general-class ranges and hatching marks the rest of the plot. Estimates confined to special classes of f are omitted.

place: Figure 1 — omitted special classes
claim: The caption excludes the convex-complement, two starlike-complement and differential-inequality subclasses from the plotted general-class ranges and cites their respective sources.

place: Theorem 1 — coefficients with a bounded weight
claim: For 0 < p < 1, f in M(p), h a Schwarz function, and e holomorphic on 𝔻 with |e| ≤ 1, the nth Taylor coefficient of e · (f∘h) has modulus at most Aₙ(p) for every n ≥ 1.

place: Theorem 1 — equality in degree two and higher
claim: For e ≡ 1 and each n ≥ 2, equality holds exactly when f = fₚ on 𝔻 and h(z) = λz for a constant λ with |λ| = 1.
source_words: equality holds if and only if $f=f_p$ and $h(z)=\lambda z$

place: Theorem 1 — equality in degree one
claim: For e ≡ 1 and n = 1, every f in M(p) attains equality with precisely the Schwarz functions h(z) = λz, |λ| = 1.
source_words: For $e=1$ and $n=1$, equality holds exactly when

place: Robertson’s terminology for the weighted class
claim: Robertson (1970, p. 3) called e · (F∘h) quasi-subordinate to F for holomorphic F, a Schwarz function h, and a holomorphic factor |e| ≤ 1. Theorem 1 gives the meromorphic coefficient estimate in this terminology.

place: Conformal radius at a finite point
claim: For a simply connected spherical domain Π omitting at least two points and finite w₀ in Π, R(w₀,Π) = |φ′(0)|, where φ maps 𝔻 conformally onto Π with φ(0) = w₀.

place: Normalization of hyperbolic distance
claim: The conformal radius is independent of the centered chart. Hyperbolic distance has curvature −4 normalization, so δ_𝔻(0,r) = artanh r for 0 ≤ r < 1.
source_words: normalized by curvature $-4$, so that $\delta_\D(0,r)=\artanh r$

place: Theorem 2 — distance to infinity
claim: When ∞ belongs to Π and w₀ = G(0) is finite, p = tanh δ_Π(w₀,∞) lies strictly between 0 and 1.

place: Theorem 2 — derivatives at the disk origin
claim: For a holomorphic map G from 𝔻 into a simply connected spherical domain Π containing ∞ and omitting at least two points, with G(0) = w₀ finite, |G⁽ⁿ⁾(0)|/n! ≤ R(w₀,Π) Aₙ(p) for every n ≥ 1, where p = tanh δ_Π(w₀,∞).

place: Theorem 2 — geometric equality criterion
claim: For each n ≥ 2, equality holds exactly when G maps 𝔻 conformally onto Π and the complement of Π is a line segment whose supporting line passes through w₀.
source_words: a line segment lying on a line through $w_0$

place: The 2008 conjectures for general targets
claim: Avkhadiev and Wirths (2008, Theorems 1 and 2) obtained the derivative estimates for targets complementary to compact convex sets. Their Conjectures 1 and 2 extend the disk-source and convex-source estimates, respectively, to general simply connected targets omitting at least two points.
source_words: one for maps on the disk and one for maps on convex domains

place: Source and target parameters for higher derivatives
claim: For meromorphic G from a proper simply connected plane domain Ω into Π and w₀ = G(z₀) finite, Rₛ = R(z₀,Ω) and Rₜ = R(w₀,Π). The parameter p equals tanh δ_Π(w₀,∞) if ∞ belongs to Π and equals 1 for planar targets.
source_words: the conformal radii of the source and of the target

place: The endpoint coefficient bound for planar targets
claim: At the planar endpoint p = 1, Aₖ(1) = k is the limit of Aₖ(p) as p increases to 1, for each k ≥ 1.

place: The binomial sum for the derivative bound
claim: For n ≥ 1, 0 < p ≤ 1, and 0 ≤ r ≤ 1, Dₙ(p,r) is the sum over k = 1,…,n of binom(n−1,k−1) rⁿ⁻ᵏ Aₖ(p), where binom denotes the binomial coefficient.

place: Closed form for the derivative bound
claim: For 0 < p < 1 and 0 ≤ r ≤ 1, Dₙ(p,r) = ((r+1/p)ⁿ⁻¹ − p²(r+p)ⁿ⁻¹)/(1−p²).

place: Theorem 3(a) — derivatives at a disk point
claim: For meromorphic G from 𝔻 into a simply connected spherical domain Π omitting at least two points, at every z₀ with finite G(z₀) and every n ≥ 2, Rₛⁿ |G⁽ⁿ⁾(z₀)|/(n! Rₜ) ≤ Dₙ(p,|z₀|), including p = 1.

place: Theorem 3(b) — derivatives on a convex source
claim: For meromorphic G from a proper convex plane domain into a simply connected spherical domain Π omitting at least two points, at every z₀ with finite G(z₀) and every n ≥ 2, Rₛⁿ |G⁽ⁿ⁾(z₀)|/(n! Rₜ) ≤ Dₙ(p,1), including p = 1.

place: Theorem 3 — sharpness of both derivative bounds
claim: Both bounds are attained for every 0 < p ≤ 1 and n ≥ 2. The extremal maps use fₚ, with the Koebe function f₁(z) = z/(1−z)² at p = 1.
source_words: Both bounds are sharp for every $p$ and $n$

place: Earlier derivative bounds by target geometry
claim: For planar targets, the disk estimate is Avkhadiev and Wirths’s 2003 Theorem 2, and the convex-source estimate is their 2007 inequality (4). Their 2008 theorems cover concave targets. Theorem 3 also covers nonconcave targets containing ∞.

place: Disk derivative bounds from earlier coefficient ranges
claim: The disk change of center and the 2009 Theorem 8.3 already give Theorem 3(a) for n = 2 at all 0 < p < 1, for n = 3 at p < 0.7, and for n ≥ 4 at p < 1/(2n−2).

place: Replacing composition by a bounded multiplier
claim: For a fixed degree n, the nth coefficient of e · (f∘h) equals that of Ef for some holomorphic |E| ≤ 1. For e ≡ 1 the polynomial form occurs in Rogosinski’s work and in Szapiel’s later reduction.

place: Removing the pole by a slit-disk chart
claim: The conformal map q from 𝔻 ∖ [p,1) onto 𝔻 fixes zero and has positive coefficients in every positive degree. With slit-disk conformal radius R = 4p/(1+p)², the pullback (f∘q⁻¹)/R belongs to S.

place: Summing the product bounds against the slit coefficients
claim: Robertson’s inequality gives |[wᵏ](FE)| ≤ k for F in S and holomorphic |E| ≤ 1. Near zero, the resulting majorant R(q+2q²+3q³+⋯) equals fₚ.

place: Duality for transfer and the classical product estimate
claim: Duality supplies the multiplier for a general weight e. Robertson’s argument gives the unweighted product estimate, and Friedland (p. 256) credits its bounded-factor extension to MacGregor.
source_words: For a general weight $e$ we prove the first step by duality

place: Recovering the base estimate from de Branges’s bound
claim: With e ≡ 1 and h(z) = z, the slit representation and |[wᵏ]F| ≤ k for F in S give |[zⁿ]f| ≤ Aₙ(p) for f in M(p) and n ≥ 1.

place: Lemma 4 — transfer of one coefficient for every germ
claim: For a Schwarz function h, a holomorphic disk weight |e| ≤ 1, and each n ≥ 0, there exists a holomorphic disk weight |E| ≤ 1 that satisfies [zⁿ](e · (g∘h)) = [wⁿ](Eg) for every g holomorphic near zero, and E(0) = e(0)h′(0)ⁿ.

place: Only the first n degrees of the germ contribute
claim: Since h fixes zero, hʲ vanishes to order at least j. Terms of g above degree n contribute zero to [zⁿ](e · (g∘h)).

place: The coefficient functional on polynomials
claim: On polynomials, the linear functional Λ(P) = [zⁿ](e · (P∘h)) satisfies |Λ(P)| ≤ ∫ |P| dσ, where σ is normalized arc measure on the unit circle.

place: The weighted coefficient as a finite sum
claim: For g holomorphic near zero with coefficients gⱼ, [zⁿ](e · (g∘h)) is the sum of gⱼ Λ(wʲ) over j = 0,…,n.

place: A harmonic majorant for the polynomial
claim: The Poisson integral U of the boundary function |P| majorizes |P| on 𝔻, and U∘h is harmonic there.
source_words: $|P|\le U$ in $\D$, and $U\circ h$ is harmonic

place: Cauchy’s estimate on an interior circle
claim: For 0 < r < 1, rⁿ |Λ(P)| is at most the normalized circle average of |P(h(rζ))|.

place: The mean value of the harmonic majorant
claim: For 0 < r < 1 the circle average of U(h(rζ)) equals U(0) = ∫ |P| dσ. Thus |Λ(P)| ≤ ∫ |P| dσ in the limit r ↑ 1.

place: A bounded density representing the functional
claim: There is a function v on the unit circle with essential supremum at most 1 such that Λ(P) = ∫ vP dσ for every polynomial P.

place: Vanishing moments above the chosen degree
claim: For every j > n, the moment Λ(wʲ) vanishes.

place: Negative Fourier modes of the shifted density
claim: For each m ≥ 1, the Fourier coefficient of wⁿv(w) at index −m is Λ(wⁿ⁺ᵐ) = 0.
source_words: has no Fourier coefficients of negative index

place: An analytic multiplier from boundary values
claim: The function wⁿv(w) on the unit circle is the almost-everywhere boundary value of a holomorphic function E on 𝔻 with |E| ≤ 1.
source_words: the boundary function of a holomorphic $E$ with $|E|\le1$

place: Taylor coefficients of the multiplier as moments
claim: For 0 ≤ j ≤ n, [wⁿ⁻ʲ]E = ∫ v(w)wʲ dσ(w) = Λ(wʲ).

place: Reassembling the coefficient of the product
claim: For every analytic germ g with coefficients gⱼ, the nth coefficient of Eg is the sum of gⱼ Λ(wʲ) over j = 0,…,n.

place: The value of the transfer multiplier at zero
claim: For every n ≥ 0 the representing multiplier satisfies E(0) = Λ(wⁿ) = e(0)h′(0)ⁿ.

place: The unweighted transfer in degree zero
claim: When e ≡ 1 and n = 0, the constant multiplier E ≡ 1 realizes the identity for every analytic germ g.

place: The unweighted transfer polynomial
claim: For e ≡ 1 and n ≥ 1, write cⱼ = [zⁿ]hʲ. The polynomial Q(w) = c₁wⁿ⁻¹ + ⋯ + cₙ satisfies [zⁿ](g∘h) = [wⁿ](Qg) for every g holomorphic near zero.

place: Positive real part of the Cayley transform
claim: For |t| = 1 the holomorphic function (1+th)/(1−th) has positive real part on 𝔻 and value 1 at zero.
source_words: positive real part and value $1$ at the origin

place: Coefficients of the Cayley transform
claim: For n ≥ 1 and |t| = 1, the nth coefficient of (1+th)/(1−th) equals twice the sum of cⱼ tʲ over j = 1,…,n, where cⱼ = [zⁿ]hʲ.

place: Carathéodory’s coefficient bound
claim: For a holomorphic function on 𝔻 with positive real part and value 1 at zero, every positive-degree coefficient has modulus at most 2.

place: The unit bound for the transfer polynomial
claim: The unweighted transfer polynomial Q has |Q(w)| ≤ 1 on the unit circle and throughout the disk.

place: Historical forms of the unweighted polynomial estimate
claim: The proof credits the unweighted polynomial argument to Rogosinski (1.1.3 and Lemma 2) and an equivalent bound to Szapiel (p. 172, (5)).
source_words: proves an equivalent bound by the subordination principle

place: Lemma 5 — the conformal slit map
claim: For 0 < p < 1, let J(z) = z+1/z, B = p+1/p and R = 4/(B+2). A conformal bijection q from 𝔻 ∖ [p,1) onto 𝔻 fixes zero and satisfies J(q(z))+2 = R(J(z)+2) as a spherical identity.

place: Lemma 5 — strict positivity in each positive degree
claim: For every n ≥ 1, the Taylor coefficient [zⁿ]q is real and strictly positive.
source_words: The coefficient of $z^n$ in $q$ is positive for every $n\ge1$

place: Lemma 5 — the extremal as a convergent series
claim: Near zero, R(q(z)+2q(z)²+3q(z)³+⋯) converges to fₚ(z).

place: Figure 2 — images of the polar grid
claim: For p = 1/2 the left panel shows circles and radii in the slit disk, and the right panel shows their images under q.
source_words: circles and radii of the slit disk (left) and their images (right)

place: Figure 2 — the boundary arc traced by the slit
claim: For p = 1/2, the two banks of the slit have boundary images on conjugate arcs meeting at 1. At the far ends of the arcs the real part tends to 7/9.
source_words: the heavy arc of the unit circle around $1$

place: Figure 2 — the role of positive slit coefficients
claim: The positive-degree coefficients of q are positive, so its powers give nonnegative weights when the coefficient estimates of Lemma 6 are summed in Proposition 7.

place: The Joukowski image of the unit disk
claim: J(z) = z+1/z maps 𝔻 one-to-one onto the sphere minus [−2,2], sending zero to ∞. On [p,1) it decreases from B = p+1/p toward 2.

place: Straightening the longer omitted interval
claim: J maps the slit disk onto the sphere minus [−2,B]. The affine map x ↦ R(x+2)−2 fixes −2 and ∞ and sends B to 2, carrying this image onto the sphere minus [−2,2].
source_words: $x\mapsto R(x+2)-2$ fixes $-2$ and $\infty$ and sends $B$ to $2$

place: Construction of the centered slit chart
claim: Conjugating x ↦ R(x+2)−2 by J gives q(z) = J⁻¹(R(J(z)+2)−2), with J⁻¹ taking values in 𝔻. The resulting conformal map fixes zero.
source_words: the affine map fixes $\infty$, and $J^{-1}$ sends $\infty$ to $0$

place: The slit-disk conformal radius
claim: At zero, q′(0) = 1/R. Its inverse χ has χ′(0) = R, the conformal radius of 𝔻 ∖ [p,1) at zero.

place: Factoring the equation for the slit map
claim: The identity z(1+q)² = Rq(1+z)² gives (q−z)(1−zq) = cz(1+q)², where c = 1/R−1 = (1−p)²/(4p) > 0.

place: A power-series recurrence for q
claim: Near zero, q = z + cz(1+q)²(1+zq+(zq)²+⋯), with c = (1−p)²/(4p).

place: The positive term in the coefficient recurrence
claim: Writing qₙ = [zⁿ]q, one has q₁ = 1+c. For n ≥ 2, qₙ is a polynomial with nonnegative coefficients in c and the earlier qⱼ, containing the term 2c times the preceding coefficient.

place: Rational form of the slit-map majorant
claim: Near zero, Rq/(1−q)² = 1/(J(z)−B) = z/(1−Bz+z²) = fₚ(z), with the value at zero supplied by continuity.

place: Lemma 6 — product with a bounded holomorphic factor
claim: For F in S and E holomorphic on 𝔻 with |E| ≤ 1, |[wᵏ](FE)| ≤ k for every k ≥ 1.

place: The normalized square root of F(w)/w
claim: For F in S, the quotient F(w)/w extends holomorphically without zeros to 𝔻. It has a holomorphic square root M with M(0) = 1, so F(w) = wM(w)².

place: The odd univalent function associated with F
claim: The function F₂(z) = zM(z²) is odd and injective on 𝔻, has F₂′(0) = 1, and satisfies F₂(z)² = F(z²).

place: Indexing the odd coefficients
claim: For each j ≥ 0, the coefficient bⱼ = [wʲ]M equals [z²ʲ⁺¹]F₂. In particular b₀ = 1.

place: Robertson’s inequality for normalized odd maps
claim: For an odd F in S with bⱼ = [z²ʲ⁺¹]F, the sum of |bⱼ|² over 0 ≤ j < k is at most k for every k ≥ 1. This follows from the Milin inequalities via the Lebedev–Milin implication (de Branges, pp. 137–138).

place: Truncating the square root at degree k−1
claim: If Mₖ is the Taylor polynomial of M through degree k−1, then [wᵏ](FE) = [wᵏ⁻¹](M²E) = [wᵏ⁻¹]((Mₖ E)Mₖ).

place: The Cauchy–Schwarz bound on the product coefficient
claim: The modulus of [wᵏ⁻¹]((Mₖ E)Mₖ) is at most the product of the Hardy H² norms of Mₖ E and Mₖ.

place: Contraction of the Hardy norm by the weight
claim: For |E| ≤ 1, the H² norm of Mₖ E is at most that of Mₖ. The squared norm of Mₖ is the sum of |bⱼ|² over 0 ≤ j < k, which is at most k.

place: Robertson’s and MacGregor’s implications
claim: Robertson observed in 1936 that the odd-coefficient inequality implies Bieberbach’s estimate. Friedland (1970, p. 256) credits MacGregor with the corresponding implication for a bounded factor E.
source_words: where it is credited to MacGregor~\cite{MacG}

place: Proposition 7 — the loss from a nonextremal weight at zero
claim: For f in M(p), E holomorphic on 𝔻 with |E| ≤ 1, and n ≥ 1, |[zⁿ](Ef)| ≤ Aₙ(p) − Rqₙ(1−|E(0)|), where qₙ = [zⁿ]q > 0 and R is the slit-disk conformal radius.

place: Pulling f back to the ordinary univalent class
claim: The inverse slit map χ avoids the pole p, fixes zero, and has χ′(0) = R. Thus F = (f∘χ)/R belongs to S.

place: Coefficients of the pulled-back weighted function
claim: For Φ = F · (E∘χ), its coefficients dₖ satisfy |dₖ| ≤ k for every k ≥ 1 and d₁ = E(0).

place: Finite coefficient expansion on the slit disk
claim: On the slit disk Ef = R(Φ∘q). For n ≥ 1, [zⁿ](Ef) equals R times the sum of dₖ [zⁿ]qᵏ over k = 1,…,n.

place: Separating the linear term of the majorant
claim: All coefficients of qᵏ are nonnegative. In the estimate for [zⁿ](Ef), the k = 1 contribution is bounded by R|E(0)|qₙ, and the terms with k ≥ 2 by Rk[zⁿ]qᵏ.

place: The full majorant and its deficit
claim: Summing Rk[zⁿ]qᵏ over k = 1,…,n gives [zⁿ]fₚ = Aₙ(p). Replacing the k = 1 term by R|E(0)|qₙ reduces the sum by Rqₙ(1−|E(0)|).

place: Transfer of the meromorphic germ in Theorem 1
claim: At each n ≥ 1, Lemma 4 applied to the germ of f at zero gives a holomorphic multiplier |E| ≤ 1 with [zⁿ](e · (f∘h)) = [wⁿ](Ef). Proposition 7 bounds this coefficient by Aₙ(p).

place: Why unweighted equality forces a rotation
claim: For e ≡ 1, E(0) = h′(0)ⁿ. Equality at any n ≥ 1 forces |h′(0)| = 1 and hence h(z) = λz with |λ| = 1.

place: Effect of a rotation on the coefficient
claim: If h(z) = λz with |λ| = 1 and aₙ = [zⁿ]f, then [zⁿ](f∘h) = λⁿaₙ. Its modulus in degree one equals 1 = A₁(p) for every f in M(p).

place: Saturation of the second coefficient after pullback
claim: If |aₙ| = Aₙ(p) for n ≥ 2, then the normalized slit pullback F satisfies |[w²]F| = 2. The term involving [w²]F in the coefficient sum has strictly positive weight [zⁿ]q².

place: Bieberbach’s second-coefficient equality case
claim: For F in S, |[w²]F| = 2 implies F(w) = w/(1−ηw)² for some |η| = 1 (Bieberbach, 1916, Satz IV, pp. 944–945).

place: Alignment of the first two Koebe coefficients
claim: For the rotated Koebe function, dₖ = kηᵏ⁻¹. Equality in the coefficient sum forces d₁ = 1 and d₂ = 2η to have the same argument, hence η = 1.
source_words: requires $d_1$ and $d_2$ to have the same argument

place: Recovering the extremal on the whole disk
claim: With η = 1 the pullback gives f = Rq/(1−q)² = fₚ on the slit disk and hence as meromorphic maps throughout 𝔻. Conversely, fₚ attains equality with every rotation h(z) = λz, including the identity.

place: Converse for each unit rotation in the proof of Theorem 1
claim: For e = 1 and n ≥ 2, the reverse implication of Theorem 1 gives equality for fₚ composed with every rotation h(z) = λz with |λ| = 1.

place: Figure 3 — the omitted segment for p = 1/2
claim: For p = 1/2, fₚ maps 𝔻 onto the sphere minus the closed real segment [−2,−2/9]. The line containing that segment passes through fₚ(0) = 0.
source_words: the sphere minus the heavy segment $[-2,-2/9]$

place: Figure 3 — images of three circles
claim: For p = 1/2, the three curves are the images under fₚ of the circles of radii 0.25, 0.70, and 0.85 centered at zero.
source_words: The curves are images of the circles $|z|=0.25$, $0.7$ and $0.85$.

place: Riemann mapping and the preimage of infinity
claim: The planar Riemann mapping theorem gives a disk chart for every proper simply connected plane domain (Rudin, Theorem 14.8). For the spherical target Π a change of coordinate gives a chart φ centered at w₀, rotatable so that φ⁻¹(∞) lies in (0,1).
source_words: after a rotation of $\D$ the point $\phi^{-1}(\infty)$ lies in $(0,1)$

place: Hyperbolic interpretation of the chart pole
claim: In the rotated chart, δ_𝔻(0,φ⁻¹(∞)) = δ_Π(w₀,∞), so φ⁻¹(∞) = tanh δ_Π(w₀,∞) = p.

place: Normalizing the spherical target chart
claim: With a = φ′(0), the function f = (φ−w₀)/a belongs to M(p), and |a| is the target conformal radius R(w₀,Π).

place: Factoring G through a Schwarz function
claim: The map h = φ⁻¹∘G is holomorphic on 𝔻 and fixes zero. At a pole of G the composition is holomorphic in the spherical coordinate at infinity.

place: The derivative as a subordinate coefficient
claim: Near zero, G = w₀ + a(f∘h). For n ≥ 1 this gives G⁽ⁿ⁾(0)/n! = a[zⁿ](f∘h) and hence the bound R(w₀,Π) Aₙ(p) for its modulus.

place: The image forced by geometric equality
claim: Equality at an order n ≥ 2 forces G to be a conformal bijection onto Π = w₀ + a fₚ(𝔻), with f = fₚ and h a rotation in its normalized factorization.

place: The omitted interval of the rational extremal
claim: With B = p+1/p > 2, fₚ = 1/(J−B) maps 𝔻 onto the sphere minus the closed interval [−1/(B−2),−1/(B+2)].
source_words: the complement of $f_p(\D)$ is the segment $[-1/(B-2),-1/(B+2)]$

place: Position of the basepoint relative to the omitted segment
claim: For an extremal target, the omitted segment lies on a line through w₀. Since w₀ belongs to the target, both endpoints lie on one ray from w₀, at distinct distances 0 < ℓ₁ < ℓ₂.
source_words: segment on a line through $w_0\in\Pi$, with endpoints at distances

place: The pole parameter from the endpoint distances
claim: For endpoint distances 0 < ℓ₁ < ℓ₂ from w₀, the model parameter p = (√ℓ₂−√ℓ₁)/(√ℓ₂+√ℓ₁) lies in (0,1).

place: Scale and direction of the extremal target chart
claim: The complex scale a has modulus 4ℓ₁ℓ₂/(ℓ₂−ℓ₁) and direction a/|a| = (w₀−ξ)/ℓ₁, where ξ is the nearer endpoint.

place: Matching the near and far endpoint distances
claim: For B = p+1/p, the scale gives |a|/(B+2) = ℓ₁ at the near endpoint and |a|/(B−2) = ℓ₂ at the far endpoint.

place: The chart onto the prescribed segment complement
claim: The affine map u ↦ w₀+au sends the omitted model interval onto the prescribed segment, matching its endpoints in order of distance from w₀. Thus w₀+a fₚ maps 𝔻 conformally onto Π.

place: Intrinsic parameters of the constructed chart
claim: The chart w₀+a fₚ sends zero to w₀ and p to ∞. Its parameter p equals tanh δ_Π(w₀,∞), and |a| equals the target conformal radius.

place: All centered charts of the extremal target
claim: For the prescribed segment complement, every conformal bijection from 𝔻 onto Π taking zero to w₀ is a disk rotation followed by the chart z ↦ w₀+a fₚ(z) and attains equality at every n ≥ 1.
source_words: composed with a rotation, and attains equality for every $n$

place: Weighted Rogosinski bound for planar targets
claim: For F in S, a Schwarz function h, and holomorphic |E| ≤ 1 on 𝔻, |[zᵏ](E · (F∘h))| ≤ k for every k ≥ 1. This gives the planar endpoint p = 1.

place: Lemma 8 — weighted coefficients in a centered source chart
claim: For meromorphic G from a proper simply connected plane domain Ω into a simply connected spherical target omitting at least two points, let G(z₀) = w₀ be finite. If φ maps 𝔻 conformally onto Ω with φ(0) = z₀ and φ′(0) = Rₛ, then H = (G∘φ−w₀)/Rₜ satisfies |[zᵏ](EH)| ≤ Aₖ(p) for k ≥ 1 and every holomorphic disk weight |E| ≤ 1. The bound includes planar targets at p = 1.

place: Target charts in the planar and meromorphic cases
claim: A centered target chart has the form ψ = w₀+af with |a| = Rₜ. When ∞ belongs to Π the chart can be rotated to put its pole at p, giving f in M(p). For planar Π the normalized f belongs to S.

place: The Schwarz factor between centered charts
claim: For centered source and target charts φ and ψ, h = ψ⁻¹∘G∘φ is a Schwarz function, and H = (a/Rₜ)(f∘h), with |a/Rₜ| = 1.

place: The two bounds for the centered coefficient
claim: For 0 < p < 1 the centered coefficient estimate follows from Theorem 1. At p = 1 the transfer and product estimates of Lemmas 4 and 6 give the bound k for degree k.

place: The disk automorphism centered at z₀
claim: The chart φ(z) = (z₀+z)/(1+conj(z₀)z) has Rₛ = 1−|z₀|² and φ⁻¹(z₀+Rₛ x) = x/(1−conj(z₀)x) near zero. Here conj(z₀) denotes the complex conjugate of z₀.

place: The local change of center in the disk
claim: Near x = 0 the map G satisfies G(z₀+Rₛ x) = w₀ + Rₜ H(x/(1−conj(z₀)x)).

place: Coefficients of the inverse disk chart
claim: For 1 ≤ k ≤ n, the coefficient of xⁿ in (x/(1−conj(z₀)x))ᵏ is binom(n−1,k−1) conj(z₀)ⁿ⁻ᵏ.

place: The disk derivative as a complex binomial sum
claim: The normalized derivative Rₛⁿ G⁽ⁿ⁾(z₀)/(n! Rₜ) equals the sum, for k = 1,…,n, of binom(n−1,k−1) conj(z₀)ⁿ⁻ᵏ [zᵏ]H.

place: The disk bound after the change of center
claim: Lemma 8 with E ≡ 1 bounds the modulus of the normalized nth derivative by Dₙ(p,|z₀|).

place: An extremal at a real disk center
claim: For z₀ = r in [0,1), the target fₚ(𝔻) and map G = fₚ∘φ⁻¹ give Rₜ = 1 and H = fₚ. All terms in the derivative sum are nonnegative, giving equality in every order n ≥ 2, also for p = 1.

place: Sharpness at every complex disk center
claim: For each fixed 0 < p ≤ 1, rotating the extremal from r to any z₀ with |z₀| = r gives a map attaining equality at that center for every n ≥ 2.

place: Normalizing a convex source chart
claim: For a centered chart φ onto the convex source, s = (φ−z₀)/Rₛ is injective with convex image, s(0) = 0 and s′(0) = 1. It has a holomorphic inverse near zero.

place: The inverse-chart germ on a convex source
claim: Near x = 0, G(z₀+Rₛ x) = w₀ + Rₜ H(s⁻¹(x)), so [xⁿ](H∘s⁻¹) equals Rₛⁿ G⁽ⁿ⁾(z₀)/(n! Rₜ) for n ≥ 1.

place: Lagrange inversion for the normalized derivative
claim: For n ≥ 1, [xⁿ](H∘s⁻¹) = (1/n)[zⁿ⁻¹](H′(z)(z/s(z))ⁿ), with the quotient extended at zero.

place: The Marx–Strohhäcker inequality for convex maps
claim: For a normalized convex univalent map s on 𝔻, Re(s(z)/z) > 1/2 throughout 𝔻, with quotient value 1 at zero (Marx, p. 62, condition (d), and Strohhäcker, p. 363, II. Satz).

place: A bounded factor in the reciprocal convex quotient
claim: The reciprocal z/s(z) lies in |w−1| < 1 and extends with value 1 at zero. It has the form 1+zv(z), where v is holomorphic on 𝔻 with |v| ≤ 1.

place: Binomial expansion of the reciprocal power
claim: The nth power (z/s(z))ⁿ is the sum of binom(n,j) zʲ v(z)ʲ over j = 0,…,n.

place: Degrees contributing after Lagrange inversion
claim: The j = n term contributes zero to degree n−1. For j < n and k = n−j, [zⁿ⁻¹](H′ zʲ vʲ) = [zᵏ⁻¹](H′vʲ).
source_words: the term with $v^n$ does not reach $z^{n-1}$

place: The Fejér mean of the analytic weight
claim: For k ≥ 1 and a holomorphic disk weight E with coefficients εⱼ, the Fejér mean Ẽ is the polynomial with terms (1−j/k) εⱼ zʲ summed over 0 ≤ j < k.

place: Fourier coefficients of the Fejér kernel
claim: For ζ on the unit circle and k ≥ 1, Kₖ(ζ) is the sum of (1−|j|/k) ζʲ over all integers j with |j| < k.

place: Positivity of the Fejér kernel
claim: For k ≥ 1 the Fejér kernel Kₖ is real and nonnegative at every point of the unit circle.

place: Unit mass of the Fejér kernel
claim: The integral of Kₖ against normalized arc measure on the unit circle equals 1 for every k ≥ 1.

place: Integral representation of the Fejér mean
claim: For z in 𝔻, Ẽ(z) is the integral of E(z conj(ζ)) Kₖ(ζ) over the unit circle with normalized arc measure dσ(ζ).

place: The Fejér mean is an admissible weight
claim: If E is holomorphic on 𝔻 with |E| ≤ 1, its polynomial Fejér mean also satisfies |Ẽ| ≤ 1 throughout 𝔻.

place: The constant term of the centered map
claim: The constant Taylor coefficient η₀ of the centered map H is H(0) = 0.

place: Coefficient convolution with the derivative of H
claim: For k ≥ 1, [zᵏ⁻¹](H′E) equals the sum of m ηₘ εₖ₋ₘ over m = 1,…,k, where ηₘ = [zᵐ]H and εⱼ = [zʲ]E.

place: The Fejér multiplier identity
claim: For k ≥ 1, k[zᵏ](H Ẽ) equals [zᵏ⁻¹](H′E). The Fejér factor on εₖ₋ₘ is m/k, giving the same summands m ηₘ εₖ₋ₘ for 1 ≤ m ≤ k.

place: The weighted derivative coefficient of H
claim: For the centered map H, k ≥ 1, and any holomorphic disk weight |E| ≤ 1, |[zᵏ⁻¹](H′E)| ≤ k Aₖ(p), including p = 1.

place: Powers of the convex-map factor as weights
claim: For 0 ≤ j < n, vʲ is an admissible weight in the derivative estimate of degree k−1 with k = n−j, including the constant weight 1 at j = 0.

place: The binomial factor in the convex-source bound
claim: For k = n−j with 0 ≤ j < n, (k/n) binom(n,j) = binom(n−1,k−1). The sum of the resulting bounds is Dₙ(p,1).

place: The extremal half-plane source
claim: The chart φ(z) = z/(1+z) maps 𝔻 onto Re x < 1/2 and has inverse x/(1−x). At z₀ = 0 the model G = fₚ∘φ⁻¹ maps onto fₚ(𝔻) with Rₛ = Rₜ = 1.

place: Simultaneous attainment on the half-plane
claim: For each 0 < p ≤ 1, the nth coefficient of x ↦ fₚ(x/(1−x)) is the sum of binom(n−1,k−1) Aₖ(p) over k = 1,…,n. This equals Dₙ(p,1), so the same map attains the convex bound in every order n ≥ 2.

place: Discussion — full coefficient bound and unweighted equality
claim: Theorem 1 gives the weighted bound. For weight one and n ≥ 2 equality requires the extremal fₚ and a rotation, and each rotation gives equality.

place: Discussion — two derivative results
claim: Theorem 3 gives both sharp derivative bounds from the stated disk and convex sources.

place: Discussion — higher-order zero bound and attainment
claim: The unrefereed expanded companion, Theorem 12, gives the bound Aₘ(p) for a zero of order at least d at 0, n ≥ d, m = floor(n/d), and the divisibility condition and example for attainment.

place: Discussion — exact maximum for (2,5)

place: Discussion — question on nondivisibility

place: Discussion — stability and sharp order
claim: The unrefereed companion, Theorems 16 and 17 with the sharpness example, gives the chordal O(√ε) estimate for n ≥ 2 at fixed p and r < 1 and sharpness of the order.
